title: Turn a script into a shot list, assembled
sub: Split the script into scenes, propose shots inside each one, then check in code that every line is covered and every shot stays inside the script and its own scene.

nodes.l: Shot list, or the gaps it found

steps.d:
1. Open on a cluttered desk at dusk...
2. A hand pulls a plain shipping box from a mailer...
...25 numbered lines in all, through 25. "One light, wherever you put it."

steps.h: Your code asks the model to split the script into scenes
steps.d:
4 scenes: INT. HOME OFFICE - DUSK (1-13), INT. HOME OFFICE - CONTINUOUS (14-15),
INT. BEDROOM - NIGHT (16-21), TAG - PRODUCT CARD (22-25)

steps.h: Your code reads the scene list back into 4 ranges
steps.d: 1-13, 14-15, 16-21, 22-25: no gap, no overlap, all 25 lines assigned to a scene

steps.h: Your code asks the model for shots across all four scenes in one call
steps.d:
20 shots proposed. Scene 2 gets two: an insert on the lamp's arm folding (line 14)
and a shot on Mara zipping the box (lines 14-15, carrying the voiceover line
that names no visual of its own)

steps.h: Your code checks coverage: every line inside a shot, every shot inside its scene and the script
steps.d:
0 uncovered lines, 0 shots dropped, 0 shots escaping their scene.
50.5s of shots across 4 scenes against roughly 137.6s to read the script aloud

steps.h: A director reads the shot list before anyone shoots it
steps.d:
sees: every shot, its scene, its line range, its estimated seconds, and the
coverage check's own report; decides whether to shoot it as drafted or send
a scene back for another pass
